title: Customize Ars your way with an Ars Pro subscription
gist: A house promotional post for Ars Technica's $25/$50 subscription tiers, whose only genuinely informative content is a publisher's admission that Google's AI search summaries have cut traffic for everyone including Ars, and that Google's 'Preferred Source' setting is now a lever publishers are asking readers to pull.

themes.theme: AI search summaries eroding publisher traffic

insights.claim: Google's AI-generated search summaries have caused a drop in referral traffic for publishers broadly, a decline Ars Technica describes as surprising no one.
insights.speaker: Eric Bangeman
insights.so_what: First-party confirmation from a publisher that AI Overviews are structurally compressing the search-referral funnel—negative for ad-funded digital media, and a driver of the shift to paid subscriptions.
insights.quote: To absolutely no one’s surprise, Google’s search-result AI summaries have led to a drop in traffic for everyone, Ars included.
insights.locator: And while we’re on the topic of journalism

insights.claim: Google now lets users designate specific websites as a 'preferred source,' which increases the likelihood of those sites' stories appearing in the Top Stories section—effectively a user-side distribution lever publishers must now campaign for.
insights.speaker: Eric Bangeman
insights.so_what: Distribution power is being re-mediated through opt-in user preferences; publishers reduced to asking audiences to manually restore their own reach.
insights.locator: Google does allow users to designate specific websites

insights.claim: Ars Technica prices its subscription at $25 for Ars Pro and $50 for Ars Pro++ per the promotion, bundling ad removal, no trackers, full-text RSS, subscriber forums, and layout customization.
insights.speaker: Eric Bangeman
insights.so_what: Benchmark for low-priced tech-media subscription tiers where the perk set is UX and ad removal rather than exclusive content.
insights.locator: And you get all of this for just $25

insights.claim: The paywalled differentiators are presentation layers—Classic view recreating the 1998 site layout and a minimalist 'Neutron Star' text-only, keyboard-navigable layout—rather than gated journalism.
insights.speaker: Eric Bangeman
insights.so_what: Signals a reader-experience-as-product strategy: monetizing power users' preference for information density instead of restricting access to articles.
insights.locator: Both Grid and List views are available for all readers
